matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides, find the numeric difference, and search for a single‑stick move that adjusts the values to balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Use when the equation is numerically imbalanced; calculate the difference and look for a stick move that changes a numeral or operator by that amount.
matchstick.example: Assuming the equation 20 = 2 - 18, trying arbitrary moves without first computing the numeric difference.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, relocate one of V’s diagonal sticks so the V becomes an X, increasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a numeral by 5 and a V is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a V but leaving the remaining shape invalid, failing to form an X.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: To change a plus sign to a minus sign, remove its vertical stick and attach it as an I to a numeral, decreasing the RHS by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce the value on one side by 1 and a plus sign is present.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from a '+' but not adding it to a numeral, leaving the plus incomplete.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains more than one I, you can remove one I (a vertical stick) from it and add that stick to another numeral, adjusting values accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase one numeral by 1 and another numeral has an extra I.
matchstick.example: Taking a vertical stick from a solitary I, causing that numeral to disappear.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: To change a minus sign to an equals sign, add a horizontal stick taken from a numeral (e.g., from an I or V) to the minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase the RHS by 1 (or otherwise adjust the operator) and a minus sign is present.
matchstick.example: Adding a horizontal to '-' from a numeral but leaving the source numeral invalid.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: To change a minus sign into a plus sign, you must supply a vertical stick from a numeral; the source numeral must remain valid after losing the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase the RHS by 1 and a minus sign is present, and you have a numeral with an extra I.
matchstick.example: Changing '-' to '+' without adding the required vertical stick, resulting in an incomplete plus sign.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: Move one horizontal stick from the equality sign to the minus sign; the equality becomes a minus and the minus becomes an equals, preserving a valid equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance can be resolved by swapping the roles of '-' and '=', and both signs are present.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' but forgetting to keep a valid '=' sign, leaving the equation without an equality.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the equality sign, you must simultaneously create a new equality sign elsewhere (e.g., by turning a minus into '=') so that the equation still contains a valid '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick from '=', ensure another '=' is formed.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from '=', turning it into '-', and not creating a new '=' sign elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears, reposition one of X’s diagonal sticks so the X becomes a V, decreasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a numeral by 5 and an X is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring that some numerals need all their sticks to stay valid.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only remove sticks from numerals that have extra sticks (e.g., II, III, or V that can become X) and ensure the source remains a valid numeral.

matchstick.description: Providing an incomplete equation after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets to preserve the required operators, especially the '=' sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Verify that the final equation still contains a valid '=', and that all operators are complete.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the minus sign as a plus sign without adding the missing component.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When turning '-' into '+', also move a vertical stick from a numeral to complete the plus sign.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model confuses stick orientations, treating diagonal sticks as vertical or horizontal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Keep stick orientations consistent: only vertical sticks can form I or part of '+', only diagonal sticks can form V or X.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the operator change but neglects the requirement for a valid equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that any stick taken from '=' is used to form another '=', or use the swap technique that preserves both signs.
